title: How to Change a Toilet Seat
summary: This Old House’s quick-guide demonstrates how to replace a toilet seat, covering seat sizing (round-front vs. elongated), accessing and removing top bolts with proper tools, and handling common hardware issues. It contrasts plastic fasteners with older brass hardware, explains why space constraints matter, and offers practical techniques such as using a basin wrench for tight spaces, a deep socket for corrosion, penetrant oil, and careful cutting with a hacksaw while protecting the porcelain with a putty knife.
topics: choosing screwdriver size to avoid damage
use of a proper blade screwdriver
deep socket use for brass bolts
bolts cutting as a last resort
putty knife as shield for china

sections.title: Choosing the correct toilet seat size
concepts: round-front seat (~16 in from back to front)
elongated seat (~18 in from back to front)
sections.description: Introduces the two common seat shapes and their back-to-front measurements to ensure the new seat fits the toilet correctly.

sections.title: Accessing and removing the top bolt
sections.description: Shows exposing the top bolt, avoiding damage by using an appropriately sized screwdriver, and beginning to loosen the bolt counterclockwise. Explains that modern plastic nuts are often wing-nuts.

sections.title: Working in tight spaces with constrained access
sections.description: Discusses how space constraints complicate removing the lower nut and introduces the basin wrench as a tool designed for tight access, with note of other compact options.

sections.title: Older brass hardware and corrosion
concepts: penetrating oil as a first-step aid
sections.description: Addresses the common difficulty of older toilets with brass hardware and corroded bottom nuts, recommending a deep socket to back off the nut and suggesting penetrating oil to break down corrosion.

sections.title: Last-resort bolt removal and porcelain protection
concepts: cutting bolt with mini hacksaw blade holder
protecting the china with a broad knife/putty knife
sections.description: If the bolt cannot be removed, demonstrates cutting the bolt off while using a putty knife or broad knife to shield the porcelain and prevent chipping or cracking.
